name: number-shape
title: Number shape
tagline: Numicon-style pegged number shapes 1–10 (2-wide, odd numbers protrude a peg) as plates, cubes or counters; derives parity, number bonds and the stem sentence.
description: Numicon-style number shapes for the numbers 1 to 10: each value laid out two units wide, filling in pairs from the bottom, so an even number is a flat-topped rectangle and an odd number has a single peg sticking out on top. You write only the value of each shape; the model derives the layout, the plate outline, the holes, the parity (odd / even), and — when two or more shapes are added — the total and an optional result shape. Render a shape as a Numicon-style coloured plate with holes (the default), or as discrete cubes or counters (the odd-even pairs column: even tops are level, the odd one sticks out). Each value carries its canonical Numicon colour. A fill-in stem sentence beneath the shapes — count, parity, or number bond — states the maths in words, with any occluded number shown as "?". Occlude a shape's numeral to ask "which number is this?", or occlude a bond total for a missing-number question. Serves recognising number shapes, odd and even, number bonds and composition by shape, and "five and a bit".
whenToUse: Reach for this for early-number work with Numicon-style number shapes (1–10): recognising the shapes, odd and even numbers, number bonds and composition by shape, doubles, and "five and a bit". Write shapes[] — one entry per shape, each just a value 1–10, laid out left to right and aligned along the bottom. Numbers are derived: never write a total or a parity word. Common configurations: recognise — one shape, show.values true (and show.parity to tag odd / even); odd and even — several shapes in a row (often piece "cubes" or "counters" — the odd-even pairs column), show.parity true, so the flat-topped evens and the bumpy odds line up for sorting; number bond by shape — operation "add", two (or more) shapes, result.show true → "6 and 4 make 10"; set result.shape true to also draw the sum as its own shape (only when the total is ≤ 10); missing number — operation "add" with one shape occluded (6 + ? = 10) or result.occlude true (6 + 4 = ?); five and a bit — a 5-shape plus a small shape (5 + 3) as a bond; composition — three or more addends (2 + 3 + 5). "Which number?" answer space — one shape with occlude true, caption asking for the number. Choose the stem sentence with stem (auto picks bond for an addition, else parity if show.parity, else a count) or turn it off with stem "none". Use piece "plate" for the holistic Numicon piece; "cubes" / "counters" for discrete units when the parity protrusion is the focus. Keep piece and stem steady across a lesson so pupils compare like with like. A staged build reads beautifully: open a bond on the first addend with the second blank, fill it a stage later, then reveal the total last. Switch model when the teaching changes: for a 2×5 ten-frame fill with two-colour counters use number/ten-frame; for a rows×columns multiplication picture use number/array; for the part-whole "cherry" use number/part-whole; for partitioning one whole into fractional parts use number/fraction-shape. Synonyms a teacher might use: Numicon, number shape, number shapes, pegged shapes, odd and even, odd or even, parity, number bond, bonds to ten, make ten, composition, partition, five and a bit, doubles.

shapes.description: The number shapes, laid out left to right and aligned along the bottom — the only quantities you author. One entry per shape; each is a value 1–10 (plus optional occlude / highlight / blank flags). Two or more shapes with operation "add" read as the addends of a number bond.

value.description: The number this shape shows, 1–10 — the ONLY quantity you author. The model lays the units 2-wide, filling in pairs from the bottom, so an even value is a flat-topped rectangle and an odd value has a single peg protruding on top. Rows, holes, the outline, the parity and the colour are all derived from this. No shape exists above ten (no canonical number-shape beyond it).

occlude.description: Render this shape's numeral as "?" — the question hook ("which number is this shape?" or a missing addend in a bond). The shape itself stays fully visible and correct, and the value is hidden as "?" in the stem sentence too, so it cannot leak. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this shape — an emphasis ring round the plate and an amber numeral. Use for the answer / the part being drawn attention to. Amber is never used as a plate colour. Default false.

blank.description: Draw this shape as a faint dashed GHOST outline of its value — no colour, no holes, no numeral — reserving its slot without filling it. For staged builds: a bond opens with the second addend blank, then a later stage fills it, so the figure never reflows. Different from occlude ("?" poses a question; blank poses nothing yet). Default false.

piece.description: How each shape is drawn. "plate" (default): the holistic Numicon-style coloured plate with circular holes and a rounded outline. "cubes": discrete stacked square cubes (the odd-even pairs column — even tops level, the odd cube sticking out). "counters": discrete round counters laid the same way. Use "plate" to recognise the piece; "cubes" / "counters" when the parity protrusion and the discrete units are the focus. The 2-wide pair-filling layout and the colours are identical — only the glyph changes.

operation.description: "none" (default): just display the shape(s) — recognise, compare, sort odd / even. "add": join consecutive shapes with "+" and show the derived total — a number bond or composition (6 + 4 = 10, 2 + 3 + 5 = 10). The total is always computed from the values; you never write it.

result.description: The derived sum line, used only when operation is "add". Both the number and (optionally) the result shape are computed from the addends — there is nowhere to write a wrong total.

show.description: Draw "= total" after the addends. Default true when operation is "add". Set false to leave the bond open (just the addends, e.g. for a "what do these make?" discussion).

shape.description: Also draw the total as its own number shape after the "=" (6 + 4 = the 10-shape). Only drawn when the total is ≤ 10 (no shape exists above ten); ignored otherwise. Default false.

occlude.description: Render the total as "?" — "6 + 4 = ?". The addends stay visible; the result shape (if any) is suppressed so the answer cannot leak. The stem sentence hides the total too. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber the total — answer emphasis. Default false.

values.description: Show each shape's numeral below it. Default true. An occluded shape shows "?" here regardless; a blank shape shows nothing.

parity.description: Tag each shape "odd" or "even" below its numeral — derived from the shape (the protruding peg). Default false. For sorting and odd / even teaching.

stem.description: Which fill-in sentence to state beneath the shapes (the verbal twin of the figure); its numbers are always derived. "auto" (default): a bond sentence for an addition, else parity if show.parity is on, else a count. "count" → "This number shape shows __." (a single shape). "parity" → "__ is an odd / even number." (a single shape). "bond" → "__ and __ make __." (the addends and the total of an addition). "none" → no sentence band. An occluded number appears as "?" in the sentence.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the stem sentence, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
